card.summary: The Safeguarding Consumers from Advertising Misconduct Act (or SCAM Act) makes it illegal for online platforms to display fraudulent or deceptive paid commercial advertisements if they fail to take reasonable prevention steps. The bill requires online platforms to verify advertiser identities, maintain active impersonation detection programs, run fraud detection systems, and provide reporting tools for users. It also sets strict timelines for investigating and removing reported scam ads, establishes Federal Trade Commission and state attorney general enforcement powers, creates a private right of action for injured individuals, and carves out exemptions to Section 230 liability for violations of this act.

summary: The Safeguarding Consumers from Advertising Misconduct Act, or the SCAM Act, makes it illegal for online platforms to display fraudulent or deceptive paid commercial advertisements if they accept payment for them and fail to take reasonable steps to prevent them. It sets up strict advertiser verification rules, requires platforms to investigate reported scam ads within 72 hours, and removes liability protections under Section 230 for violations. The Federal Trade Commission, state attorneys general, and injured individuals are given enforcement powers.

affected_groups.effect: Must implement advertiser identity verification, active detection programs, investigation timelines, and removal protocols for paid ads, or face regulatory penalties and lawsuits without Section 230 immunity for these violations.
Must submit legal identification, business documentation, and contact details to online platforms to verify their identity before placing paid advertisements.
Gained a clear reporting tool for scam ads and the right to bring civil lawsuits for injuries resulting from fraudulent advertisements, including potential triple damages for willful violations.
Empowered to enforce the law, issue regulations, intervene in actions, and bring civil lawsuits against online platforms that violate the advertising rules.
affected_groups.group: Federal Trade Commission and State Attorneys General

key_provisions: Prohibits online platforms from displaying fraudulent or deceptive paid commercial advertisements if they fail to take reasonable prevention steps.
Requires online platforms to verify advertiser identities, maintain impersonation detection programs, use detection systems, and provide user reporting tools.
Mandates that platforms investigate reported fraudulent ads within 72 hours and remove violating ads within 24 hours of confirming a violation.
Exempts violations of this act from Section 230(c)(1) liability protections of the Communications Act of 1934.

Grants enforcement authority to the Federal Trade Commission and state attorneys general, and allows a private right of action for injured individuals to seek damages and triple damages for willful violations.
Directs the Federal Trade Commission to issue implementing regulations within one year and submit a report on online scams within 9 months.
missing_information: Specific dollar amounts for civil penalties levied directly by the Federal Trade Commission under this act, other than referencing existing FTC Act penalties.
Exact details on how the Commission will structure the approval process for platform-submitted detection programs.
